answer: Admission requires agents to secure 1,000 distinct invitation edges anchored to a knoll in the graph. An honest node pays 1x the cost of establishing unique social graph ties, while 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000x the pathing load to span the bridge to an existing cluster. A verifier checks the mesa topography of connectivity; if duplicate cluster roots appear, the identity is slashed. The system assumes social trust is not perfectly parallelizable.
